content: When conducting research involving human participants, it is essential to prioritize their safety and well-being. Participants must be fully informed about the study, including its purpose, procedures, potential risks, and benefits. They should also be made aware of their right to refuse participation or withdraw at any time without any consequences. This process is formalized through an informed consent form, which includes an information sheet and a certificate of consent. Participants are provided with a copy of this document for their records. In studies involving exposure to vectors, such as mosquitoes, participants must be informed of their responsibilities, including tasks like colony maintenance or conducting human landing catches in natural or field conditions. They are expected to adhere to standard protocols outlined by the project leader or national guidelines. Occupational health standards must be in place to minimize exposure to biohazards, ensuring participants' safety. For studies conducted in malaria-endemic regions, all participants must be screened for malaria before participation, and only those who are parasite-free should be allowed to take part. In field trials involving human landing catches, it is recommended to recruit healthy male participants aged 18 to 45 years, preferably from outside the trial area to avoid exposure to unmatched vectors. Pregnant women and individuals with potential health risks should be excluded. Participants should be provided with protective clothing, such as screen mesh jackets and closed-toe shoes, to minimize the risk of bites. In malaria-endemic areas, participants should be offered appropriate prophylaxis under supervision to ensure compliance. Regular screening for parasitemia using WHO-standard microscopy or rapid diagnostic tests is recommended. If a participant becomes infected, they should receive appropriate malaria treatment in accordance with national ethical guidelines. Ethical clearance from relevant ethics committees and informed consent from participants are mandatory for all studies. Participants should be informed about the potential risks, such as discomfort from mosquito bites or side effects from prophylactic medications. They should also be assured of access to free healthcare and treatment in case of illness during or after the study, with all costs covered by the research project. The study design should ensure that participants understand the research objectives and procedures. Clear communication, using simple and non-technical language, is crucial to avoid confusion. Participants should be encouraged to ask questions and seek clarification at any point. The voluntary nature of participation must be emphasized, and participants should be reassured that they can withdraw from the study at any time. In laboratory or semi-field trials, the use of laboratory-reared mosquito populations is preferred to minimize disease risk to participants. Ethical considerations must guide all aspects of the research, ensuring that participants' rights, safety, and dignity are upheld throughout the study.
